Serpentara — Rome, Italy

Average day Higher caution advised night

In detail

Serpentara is a residential district sharing a police precinct with neighboring Fidene; press reported this precinct logs some of Rome's highest numbers of interventions for domestic abuse and drug dealing. There was also a case of a 42-year-old man barricading himself in a building and threatening to "blow everything up," and press has covered structurally unsafe, decaying ATER public housing in the area. A counter-piece argued this periphery "works and is safe," but the documented incidents above are real enough to warrant caution, especially at night.

Frequently asked questions

Is Serpentara safe?

Wandroz currently rates Serpentara in Rome as roughly average compared to other neighbourhoods in Rome during the day and an area where the data suggests extra caution relative to other neighbourhoods in Rome at night. This comes from a structured local-source assessment: an area-level review of credible local sources — local and national news, municipal and police-published material, and official surveys where they exist — consolidated across sources rather than taken from a single report. Rome publishes no comparable neighbourhood-level crime dataset; where a city does, Wandroz uses it instead.

Is Serpentara safe at night?

At night, Serpentara is rated as an area where the data suggests extra caution relative to other neighbourhoods in Rome. If you're unsure, it's worth checking recent local reviews for your specific street or block, since a neighbourhood-wide rating can't capture block-by-block variation.

Is Serpentara a good area to stay in as a tourist?

Serpentara's day rating (roughly average compared to other neighbourhoods in Rome) is the more relevant one for typical daytime tourist activity; check the night rating too if you'll be out late. The Booking.com link on this page searches Serpentara itself.

Is there official crime data for Serpentara?

Not an official government crime feed — Serpentara's rating comes from Wandroz's own current local/national press and survey research for this specific area instead (see the note on this page for what was checked and the sources used).
